title: Same working, different essence: Jansenius and the Thomists part
source_text: XLVI. Caeterum quanquam Jansenius & Thomistae recentiores in eo conveniunt quod gratia Christi, per quam homines convertuntur & bene operantur, sit gratia per se efficax, quae liberum sibi subjicit arbitrium, nequaquam vero libero arbitrio subdita est; & quae, ut effectus illius sequatur, voluntatis humanae consensum non expectat, sed consensum illum infallibiliter & potenter efficit: inter se tamen dissentiunt de gratiae illius natura atque substantia: nec eodem modo explicant qua in re consistat atque posita sit. Utrisque gratiae istius modus operandi idem est, diversa vero illius essentia.
pass_a_gloss: XLVI. However although Jansenius and the recent Thomists agree in this that the grace of Christ, through which men are converted and work well, is grace efficacious by itself, which subjects free choice to itself, but is in no way subject to free choice; and which, that its effect may follow, does not wait for the consent of the human will, but effects that consent infallibly and powerfully: yet they disagree among themselves about the nature and substance of that grace: nor do they explain in the same way in what thing it consists and is placed. To both the mode of operating of that grace is the same, but its essence diverse.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLVI. Jansenius and the recent Thomists agree that the grace of Christ by which people are converted and do good is grace efficacious of itself, which brings free choice under itself and is in no way subject to it, and which does not wait for the human will's consent for its effect to follow but brings that consent about infallibly and powerfully.

Yet they disagree about the nature and substance of that grace, and do not explain in the same way what it consists in and where it lies. For both, the way this grace works is the same; what it is differs.

lemmas.latin: de gratiae illius natura atque substantia
lemmas.gloss: about the nature and substance of that grace
the mode of operating is the same

choices.why: Kept as in I-XXX: grace whose efficacy comes from the grace itself, not from the consent that follows.
